subject: Air-gapped key broker integration review — ACME BYOK/HSM
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Air-gapped BYOK integration for Acme private deployment

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are preparing the procurement and ops plan for an on-prem private deployment in our secure data center (air-gapped). Before we proceed we'd like to validate a few design points around BYOK/HSM interaction with Redwood:

- We need an offline key provisioning flow (operator-driven) that results in an HSM-wrapped root key; Redwood should accept a sealed/imported key without requiring outbound network egress.
- Rotation: acceptable cadence is quarterly; can rotations be operator-triggered with a documented rollback?
- Audit trail: we need proof of origin for key material and a signed attestation for each import event.
- Secrets handling: are ephemeral wrapping keys supported for service account tokens and can Redwood run entirely with locally-hosted KMS endpoints?

Can your team put together a short one-page operator runbook and confirm which artifacts you can provide for our compliance team? Attaching our minimal requirements doc.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen\Security Engineering\Acme Corp
Attachment: acme-byo-qa.docx

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped BYOK integration for Acme private deployment

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we support operator-driven import of HSM-wrapped keys and a fully air-gapped private control plane. I attached a draft architecture sketch and an integration checklist for the HSM vendor. High-level notes: 

- Import flow: operator generates key material in Acme's HSM, exports a vendor-wrapped key blob and transfers it via removable media to the Redwood admin VM. The admin VM runs an import tool that verifies vendor signature, stores the key in our local KMS shim, and records a signed attestation (SHA256 + operator signature). No outbound egress required.

- Rotation & rollback: we support operator-initiated rotations. The rotation operation creates a new key version and performs a controlled key-swap on service encryption contexts; rollback is supported if operator retains previous key blobs (we recommend secure escrow in an encrypted thumb drive). We'll enumerate CLI steps in the runbook.

- Audit & attestation: Redwood will emit an import_event log with the vendor signature, operator identity, and a signed hash we can provide as PDF attestation. For SOC-style audits we can include these logs and an evidence package.

- Local KMS endpoints: Redwood Private can bind to a customer-hosted KMS API endpoint (gRPC) on the VPC. For strictly air-gapped installs we ship a KMS shim that stores keys on-disk within the customer's boundary and exposes the same API surface.

Next steps: I'll loop in Marcus for the low-level network/ops checklist and Mina for compliance artifacts. Expect the draft runbook and architecture PDF by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen\Manager, Private Deployments\Redwood Inference\Attachment: redwood-airgap-kms-arch.pdf

From: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com; Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:16:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped BYOK integration for Acme private deployment

Adding some ops-level constraints and network notes for the runbook: 

- Admin VM placement: place the import/operational admin VM on the management VLAN with no default route. The VM should have a dedicated USB port or hardware crypto-token slot for key transfer devices.
- RPMs / artifacts: all Redwood binaries for the import tool must be checksum-verified (SHA512) before execution; include offline package signatures in the bundle.
- HSM vendor connectivity: if Acme wants HSM vendor remote support, vendor access must be via an on-prem jump-host and explicit one-time support tokens; otherwise block any vendor outbound tunnels.
- Network flows: after import, the KMS shim will serve internal requests over TLS mutual auth on a private subnet (10.254.0.0/22). No NAT for the KMS host.

I've attached a stripped-down ops checklist for the data center team. Questions for Acme: do you have a FIPS 140-2/3 requirement for the HSM, and which model will you be using? That will change our acceptance tests.

Attachment: hsmco-ops-integration-guide.pdf

-Marcus

From: mina_haddad@redwood.example.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com; marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com; Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped BYOK integration for Acme private deployment

Stephanie / Marcus — this looks good. A couple of compliance asks we should include in the evidence pack: 

1) Signed attestation template: include operator name, operator key fingerprint, timestamp, and SHA256 of the imported blob. We'll fill in for the SOC report.
2) KMS ACLs & roles: record the exact role names (kms.importer, kms.operator, kms.rollback) and an example least-privilege policy.
3) Retention: logs for import_event and key_rotation must be kept for 7 years in encrypted form; include a recommended log-rotation and archival plan (SFTP/airgap vault).

Also, please coordinate with Laura for the contract section that defines responsibilities around key escrow and recovery. If Acme insists on escrow, we require a formal escrow agreement and a separate escrow KMS host configuration.

-Mina Haddad
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com; mina_haddad@redwood.example.com; laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped BYOK integration for Acme private deployment

Alice — attaching the promised artifacts: operator runbook (PDF), minimal ops checklist (PDF), and the attestation template (DOCX). Summary of deliverables for your review: 

- Operator Runbook (redwood-airgap-kms-arch.pdf): step-by-step import process, verification commands, rollback steps.
- HSM integration guide (hsmco-ops-integration-guide.pdf): vendor-specific notes, required firmware checks, and offline support model.
- Attestation & Evidence package (acme-byo-qa.docx): template attestation, log retention policy, and list of audit artifacts we will provide.

Please confirm vendor HSM model and whether you want Redwood to hold a sealed escrow copy (we will not unless contractually agreed). Once you confirm, we will schedule a 1-hour runbook walk-through with your ops team.

Thanks all — happy to run through any section in the walkthrough.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen\Manager, Private Deployments\Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-airgap-kms-arch.pdf, hsmco-ops-integration-guide.pdf, acme-byo-qa.docx
